# Let an agent do its work in your own Claude Code

## Context
Setup shows Claude Code greyed out with "coming". The approved transport design (Release 5) says an agent's worker can be a coding harness reached over ACP, and the plug-and-play design fixed how: the unmodified `claude` through the `claude-agent-acp` adapter, under a config folder of its own, never a stored token. On this Mac today: Claude Code 2.1.308, the adapter `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.106.0 (the old `@zed-industries` name is deprecated), and the Go client `github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk` v0.13.5. The built-in worker is an ADK agent whose tools run in-process; Claude Code runs in its own process with its own tools, so the task's tools have to reach it over MCP, and its file and shell tools have to be kept inside the task.

## Design
- Your own ACP agent becomes a brain you can pick for "does the work": the card is called "Your agent" and its detail says what's connected (Claude Code on your subscription, or the command set, such as `omp acp`)
  - the Setup card is live once `claude` is on PATH
    - picking it runs one test session before the choice is saved as provider `claude_code`, for the worker role only; the quick-call roles keep needing a model, as decided before
  - heyrobots runs `claude` with the owner's own sign-in (their `~/.claude`), or under its own config folder when `HEYROBOTS_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names one
    - the card shows the one command to sign in, `claude auth login` (with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=` in front when a folder is set), until `claude auth status` says signed in
    - the server's own `ANTHROPIC_*` and `CLAUDE*` variables are dropped from Claude Code's environment, so a key or token inherited by the server never replaces the owner's sign-in
    - the adapter is found on PATH as `claude-agent-acp`, else started with `npx -y` at a pinned version (needs Node 22); the command is a setting (`HEYROBOTS_ACP_COMMAND`) for people who installed it elsewhere, or who want another ACP agent such as `omp acp`, which then handles its own sign-in
  - what can go wrong: not signed in → the adapter answers "auth required" and the card says to sign in first; no answer in 90 seconds → "Claude Code didn't answer"; no Node and no adapter → the card says what to install
- A task on Claude Code is one ACP session in the task's folder
  - the executor takes the ACP path when the agent's provider, or the worker's, is `claude_code`
    - it starts the adapter, initializes, opens a session with the task folder as its working directory and the gateway as its only MCP server, and sends the same user turn the built-in worker gets (memory notes, new messages)
    - the standing instructions (worker prompt, agent section, task section) go to `CLAUDE.md` in the task folder, which Claude Code reads as project instructions and caches on its side
  - the session id is kept in the task folder
    - the next Assignment on the task loads that session so history continues, and starts a fresh one with a note when loading fails
  - the turn ends with the `report` tool as today
    - if Claude Code stops without reporting it gets one nudge, then the task is blocked with its last words as the summary
  - stopping a task cancels the session and ends the process; the run limit stays 30 minutes, and the call limit counts tool calls
  - jobs stay on the built-in worker, since an ADK workflow needs a model
    - an agent on Claude Code whose job fires runs it on the worker's model, or is blocked when there is none
  - what can go wrong: the adapter dies mid-turn → the Assignment fails with its last stderr line; the server restarts → recovery re-runs the Assignment with the loaded session, as for the built-in worker
- The task's tools reach Claude Code through a local MCP endpoint of the gateway
  - heyrobots serves one streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint on loopback
    - each session gets a random bearer token that maps to its tool set: the very tools the built-in worker would have had (toolsets, MCP servers, report and ack, memory, make_job and friends), each offered by its own schema
    - every call passes the same outward guard and taint note as today, so outward tools still become proposals and content from outside still taints the task
  - the agent's allowed skills are copied into the task folder's `.claude/skills` before the session, so Claude Code loads them itself
    - nothing else from the owner's own Claude setup is visible, since the config folder is heyrobots' own
  - Claude Code's own tools are answered through ACP permission requests, in the default (ask) mode
    - allowed: reads, searches and edits inside the task folder, and calls to the gateway's MCP tools
    - running commands is allowed only when the task holds the code or data toolset, since the owner said the Mac is theirs and trusted for now
    - refused with the reason: web fetch and search, paths outside the folder, mode switches; content from outside then arrives only through the gateway's quarantine
  - what can go wrong: a command run on the Mac reaches outside the folder → accepted for now as local trust, with the container variant from Release 5 as the next step; macOS asks for file access → the same System Settings step as for local apps
- What the worker did shows up in the trace and the chat as today
  - session updates become spans under the Assignment's worker span
    - a tool call is an `execute_tool` span with the tool's title and status; message chunks become the progress note the chat shows while the agent types
  - the ledger records nothing for Claude Code turns; the subscription is the owner's and has no price per token

## Alternatives
- The container sandbox from Release 5: safer, but the Mac is the owner's own machine now and Docker is often missing; the ACP permission gate keeps Claude Code inside the task folder, and the container can come back under the same client.
- The Claude Agent SDK directly: it would let Claude Code run heyrobots' tools in-process, but it is TypeScript-only and ties the worker to one vendor; ACP keeps Codex and Gemini CLI on the same path.
- A system prompt through ACP: the protocol has none, so the instructions would go into every user turn and defeat Claude Code's own caching; `CLAUDE.md` in the task folder is what Claude Code treats as standing instructions.

## Open Questions
- Should running commands be allowed on the Mac for a Claude Code task that holds the code or data toolset, or refused until the container variant lands?
- Should an agent on Claude Code keep a session per task, as designed, or per agent, so it remembers earlier tasks the way Claude Code remembers a project?
